comments.content: The `renderCommands` method is called three times, and each call invokes `ScriptService.replaceInternalStorage` which internally calls `taskRunner.additionalVars(runContext, taskCommands)`. This recomputes additional vars three times per execution. More importantly, `additionalVars` may include side effects (e.g., creating output directories, registering files). Consider computing additionalVars once and passing it in, or at least verify `additionalVars` is idempotent.

`renderCommands` calls `renderCommandsFromList` three times, and each call invokes `this.additionalVars(runContext, taskCommands)`. This is redundant work and may have side effects (e.g., output directory creation). Compute `additionalVars` once and reuse.

`this.renderCommands(runContext, taskCommands)` is now called both in `configure` (via `withCmd`) and again in the run method (line ~431). This means commands are rendered twice for Docker, and each render calls `additionalVars` which may have side effects. Consider rendering once and reusing.

The new overload returns `Collections.emptyList()` when `commands == null`, but the existing `replaceInternalStorage(RunContext, List<String>)` overloads may have different null-handling semantics. Verify callers relying on the new overload handle the empty-list case correctly (e.g., interpreter/beforeCommands being null should not produce empty entries in the final command list).

After this change, `this.commands` is set to the fully-composed command list (interpreter + beforeCommands + commands). Any downstream code that previously expected `getCommands()` to return only the user-provided commands (not the interpreter/beforeCommands) will now see the merged list. Verify all consumers of `TaskCommands.getCommands()` are updated accordingly.
